Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the attachments. I'll pull the event logs and the dashboard export that show how the window was marked. A couple things up front to set expectations:

- Our SLA calculation pipeline classifies an incident as a maintenance exclusion when a customer-notified maintenance with start/end times overlaps with the impact window and the impacted telemetry falls within documented maintenance scopes (control plane vs data plane paths).
- For external peering flaps, we look for corroborating evidence (BGP changes, upstream provider maintenance notices, traceroutes showing AS path drops) and then apply a third-party attribution policy. If the root cause map points to our transit partner, we typically apportion the window rather than automatically excluding it.

I'll run a quick cross-check and get you the timeline (Redwood-observed start/stop) by EOD Monday. Ben — adding you for commercial context if we need to propose a credit while we complete the technical audit. Marissa — can you take point on correlating BGP and probe data?
